syllabus_extract: Identification of AN-type, NAS etc. grip length, torques, a/c bolt identification, screws, taper pins.
specific_objectives: 9.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to describe the use of various standards, identification of bolts, nuts, safety methods and maintenance of cables.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Identification of AN-type, NAS, grip length, torques, a/c bolt identification, screws, taper pins using physical samples and torque wrenches.
intro_questions: What is the primary difference between AN and NAS fasteners?
Why is grip length critical in aircraft structural assembly?
What safety risks arise from incorrect bolt identification?

development.content:
AN-type bolt head identification
NAS bolt head identification
Grip length measurement standards
Torque specifications and application
Aircraft bolt identification codes

Screw types and applications
Taper pin identification and usage
Safety methods for fastener installation
Torque wrench calibration checks
Marking and traceability procedures

Common errors in bolt selection
Maintenance of cable fasteners
Documentation of torque values
Inspection criteria for worn pins
Storage and handling protocols

summary_questions: Explain the significance of the AN-470 series in aircraft structures.
Describe the procedure for verifying taper pin integrity before installation.
How do you ensure torque values are recorded correctly for maintenance logs?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report comparing AN and NAS fastener standards, highlighting key identification features and torque requirements for the next lesson on nuts and turn buckles.

pft_rows.syllabus: Nuts, miscellaneous nuts, washers, Safety methods for turn buckles and various types of turn buckles.
